newsitem.title: UK: Cash Brent spreads, North Sea differentials steady.
newsitem.headline: Cash Brent spreads, North Sea differentials steady.

text.p: Prompt intermonth cash Brent values steadied on Tuesday afternoon after early slippage but short term CFD swaps slipped.
May/June Brent traded again at -29 and -30 cents before firming to -25/-27 cents after an initial five cents loss from Monday's levels ahead of expiry on the IPE at close of business on Tuesday.
CFDs for next week traded at June -65 cents, down a few cents from deals earlier in the day.
Physical differentials were steady in a market still more interested in finishing off end of April barrels before slicing into early May cargoes.
Forties for April 29-May 1 traded unchanged at Dated Brent plus six cents. Sellers said they would ask more for early May cargoes. Buyers thought they could pay less.
"There's more of a comfort zone for early May than end April so we're hoping to move up a few cents," a Forties seller said.
Brent traders said transatlantic sales had helped clear out the overhang of April barrels, but differentials showed no sign of further improvement.
Rumours of an April 26-28 sale at May -50 cents could not be immediately confirmed.
A European major last week sold two cargoes into the Louisiana Offshore Oil Port (LOOP) at around June WTI -$1.00. The Brents were destined for Canada and more were on offer this week, traders said.

The May Brent programme released on Tuesday scheduled the equivalent of 41.8 cargoes, or two full 500,000 barrel cargoes more than the revised April programme. Traders said the higher programme was due to the longer month and a slightly lighter maintenance schedule on the Brent system than in April.

Mediterranean markets were quiet with refiners slow to pay the firmer levels following Urals deals around dated -$1.15 at the end of last week. Offers were thin and refiners expected the differential to firm before May loading barrels started to emerge.
"Then there will be some decent competition for Urals. Cheaper Kirkuk in May should knock 10-20 cents off Urals," one refiner said.

Negotiations continued between Syrian State oil company Sytrol and term customers over May term prices. Syrian Light was being negotiated at dated Brent -90/-82 cents while discussions on Souedie were 10 cents apart at dated Brent -$4.70/-$4.60 a barrel. New prices were not expected to be settled until early next week.

West African markets saw lots of third decade Qua Iboe still unsold and talk around dated Brent +5/10 cents. At least two VLCCs of Forcados remained for sale in the third decade of April. The grade was assessed around dated Brent -30/-25 cents.
Buying interest continued from the Far East though sellers said a heavy maintenance programme there was slowing business down.
"It's just ploughing along. Selling price is a matter of getting the right person at the right time. Some grades could be plus or minus ten cents from last done," one seller said.
